newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares retreat from session high to close level.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares retreat from session high to close level.

text.p: * NZ shares back down from session high to end level
* Warehouse eases after annual meeting
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
327 +4 * NZSC cap index +15.64 at 4,904.42
368 nil * Volume NZ$61.1 million. Futures untraded
745 -3 * Other movers - -7 +5
New Zealand shares retreated from session highs on Wednesday to close almost exactly square on reasonable turnover.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended just over half a point up at 2,356.83 on turnover worth NZ$61.1 million.
Volume was boosted by line of 7.10 million Fletcher Forest shares at NZ$2.29 each, done through Hendry Hay McIntosh.
A line of a million shares in FCL Paper, transacted at NZ$2.57 a share, was done through ANZ Securities.
Telecom struggled, despite strength on the bond market, and Tim Snedden at ANZ Securities said the decline may have been brought on by currency weakness.
"For a long time Telecom has been almost a currency play for the overseas investor where they can get exposure to New Zealand and exposure to the currency at the same time," Snedden said.
Carter Holt Harvey ended four cents stronger at NZ$3.27 after favourable reports from a brokerage on pulp and paper.
Air New Zealand A and B shares were actively traded as switching between the two intensified.
Cut price retailer The Warehouse fell seven cents to NZ$3.23 after the annual meeting, where the company said sales in November had been erratic.
Optimism about a strong result from Owens Group proved well-founded, the stock maintaining its five cent gain to close at NZ$2.25.
The transport group reported a slight lift in first half profit to NZ$4.93 million and said the full year was likely to be the about the same as the previous year's.
Steel and Tube retraced 20 cents to NZ$8.80 after a strong run on Tuesday.
